title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber
talk_summary: Uber describes six shared building blocks (model gateway, MCP gateway, agentified devpods, skills marketplace, context graph, assistant surface) that let thousands of engineers run agents end-to-end through the SDLC. They then show a feature moving from idea to PR to maintenance, with validation and review shifted into the inner loop and a managed loop surface for maintenance skills.

takeaways.technique: MCP gateway with CLI projection and code-mode skills
takeaways.what_they_do: One gateway fronts all internal and SaaS MCPs; they project MCPs into a CLI pattern so responses don't consume context, and auto-install a 'code mode' skill that generates Python scripts for the heaviest token-consuming MCP use cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we projected all of these MCPS into CLI pattern so that even the response doesn't eat up in your context

takeaways.technique: Unified context graph instead of per-system MCP lookups
takeaways.what_they_do: They consolidated scattered context (services, ownership, deps, design docs, Jira, incidents) into one graph with 150 node/edge types so agents find context in one hop rather than burning tokens across 20-30 systems.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This burns tokens. This adds a lot of latency and it creates more unpredictable outcomes.
takeaways.numbers: 150 node/edge types; 40M entries; 'massive improvement in tokens, turns and latency'

takeaways.technique: Shift validation and cheap review into the inner loop before CI
takeaways.what_they_do: Autonomous agents stop at a draft PR and self-validate first: static analysis, simulator screenshots compared to Figma, frontend+backend staging integration; a smaller/faster model does inner-loop review while a stronger model does deeper outer-loop review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can have a smaller model that runs uh faster with a with a with a medium model

takeaways.technique: Self-healing CI and evidence table on autonomous PRs
takeaways.what_they_do: CI failures are auto-fixed by agents, and autonomous diffs carry a table listing every check they passed (including screenshots) so human reviewers trust the diff went through self-improvement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: on the PR, you will have a table attached that says all these different checks that it went through, including the screenshots

takeaways.technique: Managed loop surface for maintenance skills
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of letting thousands of ad-hoc cron loops proliferate, they have one managed surface to enroll services into maintenance skills (e.g. feature-flag cleanup), scheduled when CI capacity is high, with diff volume capped and accept/reject labels fed back to improve the skill.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We don't want thousands of loops being set up across the company without any bounds.

takeaways.technique: Skills marketplace with lint and automated review
takeaways.what_they_do: Core and domain skills go into a managed marketplace with lint checks and automated review to enforce baseline quality, plus one-command discovery/install and persona-based auto-install.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it goes through a whole bunch of lint checks, automated reviews which ensures a baseline skill quality
